entries.claim: The new spine sentence says that on a project under Cadence Seldon "reads the code with Read, Glob and Grep only". The recorded runs show this is false. The spine step on spine-who-relies and spine-conventions makes a Bash listing call every time. The same diff's grant sentence at README.md:69 admits that read-only shell commands get through, so the README contradicts itself.
entries.failure_scenario: Run the README's own eval command. Plan 8's full-suite audit (.planning/phases/6/records/reports/plan-8.md lines 7 and 10, open item 2) shows the spine step in spine-who-relies ran `ls -la /tmp/claude-eval-r86agU/home/cwd`. Plan 7's runs (reports/plan-7.md lines 11, 16, 19, 20, 24) show it ran `git ls-files; ls -la` and `ls -la; ls -la .planning .planning/seldon; git ls-files | head -100` on spine-who-relies and spine-conventions. Each time the permission layer accepted the call as `subcommandResults`. SKILL.md section 15 (lines 854-856) only instructs "Read, Glob and Grep only, never a shell command". The Plan 7 report (line 51) records that this prose did not stop the call, and nothing in the harness enforces it. A user reading line 51 will think the spine step cannot run shell commands against their code, but in practice it does. The sentence should describe the instruction or the observed behavior truthfully, not state as fact a guarantee the runs have already broken.
